literal.prompt: Ледник движется за счёт деформации льда и скольжения у ложа; скорость у поверхности может отличаться от скорости у основания. Какой полевой метод позволяет оценить скорость поверхностного потока по движению отдельных маркеров?

literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC describes glacier movement as internal ice deformation plus basal sliding (L77-L79), notes that friction slows movement at the underside relative to the surface (L101-L103), and separately documents GPS stake surveys used to calculate ice velocities (GPS page L68-L69). This prompt therefore asks the field method for the surface-flow quantity in a glacier with depth-varying flow. The other complete options describe paleoclimate records from cores, radar sounding of subglacial targets, and satellite height observations.
literalGroups.locator: NSIDC glacier science L77-L79,L101-L103,L200-L201; GPS dataset L68-L69,L88-L95; BAS AGAP L24,L116-L120; NOAA L114,L143.

literalGroups.literal: Лёд движется благодаря внутренней деформации и скольжению по ложу. Повторные GPS-наблюдения стальных измерительных стержней показывают скорость поверхностных маркеров, которая может отличаться от скорости у основания.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC says glacier flow includes internal deformation and basal sliding (L77-L79), and that friction can make the underside move slower than the surface (L101-L103). Its GPS field-survey dataset records measurements of steel stakes and calculated vertical and horizontal velocities (GPS page L68-L69,L88-L95).
literalGroups.locator: NSIDC glacier science L77-L79,L101-L103; GPS dataset L68-L69,L88-L95.

literalGroups.literal: В Аллан-Хиллс повторные GPS-измерения стальных измерительных стержней позволили рассчитать горизонтальную и вертикальную скорости льда.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC reports high-precision GPS measurements of steel stakes in the Allan Hills and says the repeated survey interval permitted horizontal and vertical ice velocities to be calculated (L68-L69).

literalGroups.primaryGround: NSIDC says ice cores provide continuous climate records and that air trapped in them reveals past atmospheric composition and other climate information (L200-L201).

literalGroups.primaryGround: BAS states that airborne radar together with satellite measurements helped locate more than 200 Antarctic subglacial lakes (L24), and lists airborne radio-echo sounding data on bed and surface elevation (L116-L120).

literalGroups.literal: ICESat-2 измеряет высоту поверхности ледникового щита; по этим данным оценивают изменение его массы.

fourFullPromptAnswerNoteAssessments.plausibilityUniqueKeyAndNoteTruthUsefuln: The prompt is grammatical and describes a glacier-specific kinematic situation: deformation and basal sliding produce flow, while surface and basal speeds can differ. GPS geodesy uniquely gives repeated positions for surface markers; altimetry measures surface height, radar sounding probes buried features, and ice-core analysis reconstructs climate. The revised row distinguishes four plausible ice-study methods; the note is true and contributes an Allan Hills result beyond the prompt.
